title: fix(deps): move @kaipu/domain to dependencies where runtime code needs it
body:
## What

`packages/application` and `packages/infra-db` declared `@kaipu/domain` as a **devDependency** while importing runtime values from it (error classes, constants, mapper functions), not only types. This moves it to `dependencies` in both packages. `packages/infra-storage` imports only types from `@kaipu/domain`, so it stays a devDependency.

## Why

It only works today because bun workspaces hoist every package into one shared `node_modules` and nothing prunes devDependencies at install time. `bun install --production`, publishing either package, or a stricter installer would leave `@kaipu/domain` missing at runtime and break both packages.

## Status

- The original commit `4c19a94c` is from 2026-09-20. The branch existed only locally until today.
- `main` was merged in (`fedb69ea`), with no rebase or force push. The only conflict was `bun.lock`: I took `main`'s lock and regenerated it with `bun install`. Against `main`, it now differs only in the `@kaipu/domain` move. It also updates three stale `version` fields (`kaipu-record`, `server-hono`, `web-hono`) that `main`'s lock had left behind the `package.json` files.
- Verified locally: `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, plus `check-types`, `build` and `test` for `@kaipu/application`, `@kaipu/infra-db` and `server-hono`. All 12 turbo tasks pass.

## How to test it yourself

1. Check out the branch and run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. It must succeed with no lockfile change.
2. Run `grep -n '@kaipu/domain' packages/application/package.json packages/infra-db/package.json`. Both lines must be under `"dependencies"`.
3. Run `bun run build` and `bun run test` from the root. Expect the same result as on `main`.
